title: When Do Plants Flower? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
The same bushes on Aarav's bicycle road burst into flowers in the same month every year, and some seeds lie in the soil for months without sprouting. He asks: how does a plant know the season, and why do some seeds wait?

This topic is not in the current NCERT text but is in the ISC syllabus. We see what photoperiodism means, zoom from the whole plant to the leaf and the flowering signal, and follow day length to a flower step by step. Then long day, short day and day neutral plants with the critical duration, vernalisation with spring and winter wheat, biennials and a pause and think, a worked example on why a seed waits (dormancy, its causes and fixes), the exam trap about the shoot tip, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 95 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Why plants flower on time
0:38 What is photoperiodism?
1:00 Zoom ladder: plant, leaf, signal
1:27 Day length to flower, step by step
1:58 Long day, short day, day neutral
2:17 Vernalisation: spring vs winter wheat
2:40 Why cold matters + pause and think
3:12 Worked example: seed dormancy
3:46 Exam trap: who senses day length?
4:06 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:33 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System. How does a fish breathe in water, an insect through tiny tubes, and you through your nose?
